description: Works out the costs a self-represented party can claim in the civil courts of England and Wales under CPR 46.5: £24 an hour for time spent on or after 1 October 2025 and £19 an hour before (PD 46 para 3.4), or proven financial loss; payments for legal services and expert help with the costs claim; disbursements; the two-thirds cap on everything except disbursements, checked only against your own figure for what a lawyer would have been allowed; the small claims track limits (CPR 27.14(2)); fixed recoverable costs (CPR 45.4); and who counts as a litigant in person. It never estimates what a lawyer would have been allowed, and the court decides the time reasonably spent.

comparator.description: Your own figure for what a legal representative would have been allowed (for "frc", the fixed recoverable costs), to check the two-thirds cap, in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

costsExpert.description: Paid for expert help with the costs claim, in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

costsExpertQualified.description: That expert is in a PD 46 para 3.1 class: a barrister, solicitor, FCILEx, FACL, or a costs draftsman in the Academy of Experts or the Expert Witness Institute.

counsel.description: Direct-access counsel's fees actually paid, in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

courtFees.description: "small-claims": court fees paid, in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

disbursements.description: Other disbursements: court fees, travel, witness and expert witness fees, in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

earnings.description: "small-claims": lost earnings, one entry per person per day (each capped at £95), each in pounds, e.g. ["120", "95.50"]. In a query string, leave out thousands separators.

experts.description: "small-claims": experts' fees, one entry per expert (each capped at £750), each in pounds, e.g. ["120", "95.50"]. In a query string, leave out thousands separators.

hoursAfter.description: Hours of your own time spent on or after 1 October 2025 (£24 an hour), as a number such as "12.5" or hours and minutes such as "3:30".

hoursBefore.description: Hours of your own time spent before 1 October 2025 (£19 an hour), as a number such as "12.5" or hours and minutes such as "3:30".

injunction.description: "small-claims": the claim includes an injunction or specific performance.

injunctionAdvice.description: "small-claims" with injunction: paid for legal advice on that claim (capped at £260), in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

legalServices.description: Paid for legal advice or help from a lawyer qualified in England and Wales, in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

provenLoss.description: Financial loss you can prove for the time spent, instead of the hourly rate, in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

regime.description: What kind of claim: "general" (costs not fixed: multi-track, a fast track claim outside fixed recoverable costs, an application, or costs-only proceedings), "small-claims" (the small claims track), "frc" (fixed recoverable costs, CPR 45 Sections VI to VIII), "section-2" (fixed costs on issue, judgment or enforcement, CPR 45 Section II).

sameDayWitness.description: A witness allowance is claimed for a day also claimed as attendance time.

travel.description: "small-claims": reasonable travel and overnight expenses, in pounds, e.g. "12500" or "12,500.50".

unreasonable.description: "small-claims": the court found a party behaved unreasonably (CPR 27.14(2)(g)).

who.description: Who is claiming the costs: "individual" (an individual acting for themselves), "company" (a company acting through a director or employee who is not its lawyer), "lawyer-outside" (a lawyer acting in person outside their own practice, e.g. an employed solicitor or a barrister), "lawyer-own-practice" (a solicitor acting through their own practice: a sole practitioner, a partner, or an LLP), "company-in-house" (a company acting through its in-house solicitor).
